events.title: The Glance
events.text: At a party, {person:partner} noticed me noticing someone. The drive home is quiet.

choices.label: Take their hand and reassure them
choices.outcome_text: I told them they are my favourite view, and I meant it.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.outcome_text: My almost-affair joke landed softly and died quickly.

choices.label: Snap that they are being paranoid
choices.outcome_text: My question about the late texts came out too sharply, and we both heard it.

events.title: The Late Message
events.text: {person:partner}'s phone lit up at midnight with a name I don't know and a flame emoji.

choices.label: Ask about it in the morning, calmly
choices.outcome_text: It was a colleague. I slept better for having asked.

choices.label: Look through the phone while they shower
choices.outcome_text: I checked their phone and found nothing, and I hated myself a little for looking.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.outcome_text: I said nothing about the strange texts, and the question kept me company all week.

events.title: A Name From Before
events.text: {person:ex} sent a friend request and a message: 'Saw your name today. Thought of you.'

choices.label: Reply politely and close the door
choices.outcome_text: I wrote 'good to hear from you — take care' to my ex and left it there.

choices.label: Agree to catch up over coffee
choices.outcome_text: The coffee was fine. The look on my face when I got home was not.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.outcome_text: Some doors to an ex stay closed for a reason.

events.title: Working Late
events.text: I said I was working late. {person:partner} saw me across the café, laughing with {person:other}, before I saw them.

choices.label: Admit everything right there
choices.outcome_text: I confessed the almost-affair out loud, and the café got very quiet.

choices.label: Deny and deflect
choices.outcome_text: The lie about my evening came out fast. It did not fit well.

choices.label: Follow them home and explain
choices.outcome_text: I chased the silence all the way home.

events.title: The Close Call
events.text: {person:partner} came home an hour early. I was not quite where I said I would be.

choices.label: Offer a half-true version
choices.outcome_text: I told my partner the part that was true and skipped the rest.

choices.label: Change the subject fast
choices.outcome_text: We changed the subject at dinner. My conscience did not.

choices.label: Come clean, unprompted
choices.outcome_text: The confession was smaller than the fear of keeping the secret.

events.title: The Line I Didn't Cross
events.text: Something almost happened last weekend. Nothing did, but it almost did, and it is sitting on my chest.

choices.label: Confess the almost
choices.outcome_text: I told them the secret, and the telling made it smaller.

choices.label: Carry it alone
choices.outcome_text: I carried the almost-mistake alone, and the secret quietly weighed on me all year.

choices.label: Make it a joke that isn't a joke
choices.outcome_text: I tried to joke away the almost-affair; my partner laughed, but I could not.

events.title: I Need to Tell You Something
events.text: {person:partner} sits down very carefully and says there was a kiss, once, at a conference, and it has been eating them alive.

choices.label: Forgive, honestly
choices.outcome_text: I forgave them, and some of the weight moved off us both.

choices.label: Ask for time and space
choices.outcome_text: I needed the guest room and three quiet days.

choices.label: Talk all night until it makes sense
choices.outcome_text: We talked until the kettle was empty twice.

events.title: Helpful Comments
events.text: {person:partner}'s mother has spent the entire dinner explaining how she would run my marriage.

choices.label: Charm offensive: wine and compliments
choices.outcome_text: I won the evening. It cost a bottle and most of my patience.

choices.label: Smile and endure it
choices.outcome_text: My smile held until the car park.

choices.label: Set a gentle boundary
choices.outcome_text: It was polite, firm, and the dessert course was frosty.

events.title: How Are We, Really?
events.text: {person:partner} suggests the check-in we promised each other: an honest talk about how our arrangement is working — no judgement, either way.

choices.label: Be completely honest, even the awkward parts
choices.outcome_text: Consent kept honest is what makes us work, and I said so out loud.

choices.label: Suggest recommitting to just each other
choices.outcome_text: We talked about closing the door, and either way, it was our choice.

choices.label: Not tonight — postpone the talk
choices.outcome_text: The talk we were both avoiding waited. It did not disappear.

events.title: Full Transparency?
events.text: {person:partner} proposes a phones-open policy. Everything, anytime, nothing to hide.

choices.label: Agree — open books
choices.outcome_text: I handed over my passcode and felt lighter.

choices.label: Share the important things, keep some privacy
choices.outcome_text: We drew a line we could both live behind.

choices.label: Refuse on principle
choices.outcome_text: Trust built from surveillance isn't trust, I said. They heard it.

events.title: In Front of Everyone
events.text: A disagreement about nothing became an argument about everything, in the middle of the street.

choices.label: Suggest you both walk it off
choices.outcome_text: Ten minutes apart saved the evening.

choices.label: Make up right there, deliberately
choices.outcome_text: I apologised first, loudly, on the pavement, and meant it.

choices.label: Let it boil over
choices.outcome_text: We gave the street a show neither of us wanted.

events.title: Just a Friend
events.text: {person:partner} has started asking pointed questions about my oldest friend.

choices.label: Introduce them properly
choices.outcome_text: I introduced my oldest friend to my partner properly; they got along and the pointed questions stopped.

choices.label: Reassure, patiently
choices.outcome_text: I patiently explained the twenty-year history with my oldest friend, and my partner finally listened.

choices.label: Keep my friend and my partner apart
choices.outcome_text: Keeping the peace cost me a lunch I had wanted.

events.title: Go Public With Us?
events.text: {person:lover} is tired of being a secret and asks, plainly, to be acknowledged.

choices.label: Agree to go public
choices.outcome_text: I held their hand where everyone could see. It felt like air.

choices.label: Ask for more time
choices.outcome_text: They said they understood. Their face said less.

choices.label: End the secrecy by ending it
choices.outcome_text: I let them go, and it was kinder than keeping them hidden.

events.title: Around the Water Cooler
events.text: A colleague 'heard things' about my marriage and would love to confirm the details.

choices.label: Laugh it off gracefully
choices.outcome_text: When my colleagues pressed me for gossip about my own life, I gave them nothing and kept my smile.

choices.label: Shut it down, firmly
choices.outcome_text: The work water cooler went quiet for a week after I gave the gossip nothing.

choices.label: Say nothing at all
choices.outcome_text: Rumours starve fastest on a diet of silence.

events.title: It's Out There Somehow
events.text: The thing I hoped would stay private is being whispered about at the market.

choices.label: Own it with your chin up
choices.outcome_text: When the rumour about my marriage spread, I confirmed it myself and took its teeth.

choices.label: Deny everything
choices.outcome_text: Denial is a debt that comes due.

choices.label: Be conspicuously above it
choices.outcome_text: I bought my bread at the gossiping bakery, held my head high, and left.

events.title: The Date I Forgot
events.text: {person:partner} is being too kind about the date that I absolutely, completely forgot.

choices.label: Grand gesture, immediate
choices.outcome_text: For our anniversary: flowers, dinner, and a handwritten page. I will not forget again.

choices.label: Apologise honestly, no props
choices.outcome_text: I said sorry like I meant it, which I did.

choices.label: A belated card and a joke
choices.outcome_text: The apology joke softened the fight. Only a little.

events.title: Paradise, With Receipts
events.text: Day three of the trip and {person:partner} and I are arguing about what everything costs.

choices.label: Throw the budget overboard
choices.outcome_text: The sunset cruise fixed what arithmetic broke.

choices.label: Rebuild the budget together over breakfast
choices.outcome_text: Over breakfast, my partner and I rebuilt our trip budget in a spreadsheet, and it saved the holiday.

choices.label: Sulk by the pool
choices.outcome_text: The pool was lovely. The silence wasn't.

events.title: One Table, Two Partners
events.text: Tonight both {person:partner} and {person:lover} are at my table, and the atmosphere has a pulse.

choices.label: Play thoughtful host all evening
choices.outcome_text: By dessert they were laughing at the same jokes. I exhaled.

choices.label: Pay more attention to one of them
choices.outcome_text: I felt the temperature drop from across the table.

choices.label: Retreat to the kitchen to 'check the oven'
choices.outcome_text: The oven was fine. I checked it four times.

events.title: The Invitation
events.text: {person:ex} is getting married, and the invitation arrived addressed to both of us.

choices.label: Attend together, hand in hand
choices.outcome_text: I toasted their future and meant every word.

choices.label: Decline gracefully
choices.outcome_text: A kind card and no complications.

choices.label: Go alone 'for old times' sake'
choices.outcome_text: An ex offering old times' sake is a door best left shut.

events.title: Quiet Repair
events.text: {person:partner} suggests a weekend away — no phones, no errands, just us, to remember why we chose this.

choices.label: Book the quiet cabin
choices.outcome_text: Two days of slow mornings put us back together.

choices.label: Do it at home: phones off, door locked
choices.outcome_text: We stayed in like teenagers and talked until two.

choices.label: Not this month — life is too loud
choices.outcome_text: The calendar won. We both lost.
